dict.Tenue, elle bloque toutes les attaques s: Held, it blocks every attack except the heavy lunge and claws, which break it; the blade follows the enemy point on its own, high or low. Raised just before the hit, it is a perfect parry (window of 0.32 s on Easy, 0.24 s on Normal, 0.14 s on Hard): the enemy blade is swept aside and the Attack button becomes Riposte for 0.45 s. On Easy and Normal, the enemy point glows red when you must raise your guard, and a golden ring guides the perfect riposte (zone from 0.10 to 0.30 s on Easy, 0.12 to 0.26 s on Normal, 0.13 to 0.22 s on Hard). Mashing the guard never opens a perfect parry.
dict.Quand les lames se touchent au repos, le: When the blades touch at rest, the steel is engaged (« STEEL ENGAGED »). Steel engaged, hold → to push their blade: whoever pushes longest dominates the steel (their next blow is slower, yours instant). The guard loses to the beat, the bind and the heavy lunge; the direct attack loses to the opposition of a bind and to the parry; the beat and the bind lose to the evasion (disengage, compound) and to retreat; the evasion loses to the guard.

dict.Estoc porté main haute, la pointe plonge: A thrust delivered hand high, the point plunging over the enemy blade. Slower than the stoccata, it passes over a guard held too low.
dict.La distance d'où l'on peut toucher en se: The distance from which one can hit by lunging. Capoferro distinguishes wide measure (you must lunge) and narrow measure (the arm is enough). All rapier fencing begins with it.
dict.Au début du XVIIe siècle, la parade de r: In the early 17th century, the rapier parry is usually made with the strong of the blade, covering the attacked line, ideally at the last moment so as to follow on at once.
dict.L'attaque qui suit immédiatement une par: The attack that immediately follows a parry, while the opponent is still committed to his own. The French word comes from the Italian risposta, « answer ».
dict.Menacer une ligne pour faire parer, puis: Threaten one line to draw a parry, then strike in the one that opens. The Italian treatises warn: a feint that is too slow becomes a gift to the opponent.
dict.Un coup sec sur la lame adverse pour l'é: A sharp blow on the enemy blade to knock it aside before attacking. It opens the line, but strikes thin air if the opponent evades in time.
dict.Lames en contact, l'escrimeur sent la pr: Blades in contact, the fencer feels the opposing pressure and pushes at the right moment to take the strong on the weak. Dominated steel leaves the line open.
dict.Se dérober à un battement ou une prise d: Evade a beat or a bind
dict.Passer la pointe sous la lame adverse po: Pass the point under the enemy blade to escape its contact. Against the beat and the bind, it is the natural answer: the opponent finds only thin air.
dict.Frapper dans le temps de l'attaque adver: Strike in the tempo of the enemy attack, during its preparation. Counter-time is the weapon of patient fencers: it punishes those who wind up too wide.
dict.La passe sous la lame · passata sotto: The pass under the blade · passata sotto
dict.Esquive décrite par les maîtres italiens: A dodge described by the Italian masters: the body plunges under the enemy thrust, the free hand rests on the ground, and the point rises toward the chest. Spectacular and risky.
dict.Le pied arrière tourne et efface le corp: The rear foot turns and takes the body off the line, while the point stays forward. The Italians would later call this move inquartata.
dict.La rapière est d'abord une arme d'estoc,: The rapier is first a thrusting weapon, but it keeps an edge. A heavy cut delivered from above can force a guard held too stiffly.
dict.Maître siennois. Son Gran Simulacro dell: Sienese master. His Gran Simulacro dell'arte e dell'uso della scherma, published in Siena in 1610, is one of the great rapier treatises: measure, tempo and lunge are described with precision.
dict.Maître padouan au service du roi du Dane: Paduan master in the service of the King of Denmark. His treatise De lo schermo overo scienza d'arme appeared in Copenhagen in 1606; it shows very low guards and passes under the blade.
dict.Affronter un escrimeur de la destreza: Face a fencer of the destreza
dict.École fondée par Jerónimo Sánchez de Car: School founded by Jerónimo Sánchez de Carranza (De la filosofía de las armas, 1582), then Luis Pacheco de Narváez (1600). Arm extended, geometry of steps around an imaginary circle, control of the enemy blade.
dict.Son Académie de l'Espée, publiée en 1630: His Académie de l'Espée, published in 1630, transposes the destreza into huge engravings where fencers walk on a circle drawn on the floor. The circle of the Spanish hall in chapter 4 is a tribute to it.
dict.Se battre au bord de la Seine, la nuit: Fight on the banks of the Seine, at night
dict.Achevé en 1607, c'est le premier pont de: Completed in 1607, it is the first bridge in Paris without houses. The equestrian statue of Henri IV was placed there in the 1610s. By day, everything is sold there; by night, people are robbed.
dict.L'île de la Cité est alors un entassemen: The Île de la Cité is then a jumble of tall, narrow houses around the Palace and Notre-Dame. The slate roofs form a second Paris, that of thieves and cats.
dict.Richelieu fait bâtir son palais près du: Richelieu had his palace built near the Louvre from the late 1620s. Bequeathed to the king on his death, it would become the Palais-Royal.
dict.La cathédrale de l'île de la Cité, achev: The cathedral of the Île de la Cité, completed in the 14th century. In 1633, its bells still set the rhythm of all Paris.
dict.Inaugurée en 1612 (aujourd'hui place des: Inaugurated in 1612 (today the Place des Vosges), the most elegant square in Paris. It is there, in 1627, that the Count of Bouteville fights a duel in broad daylight, in defiance of the edict.
dict.En février 1626, un édit de Louis XIII,: In February 1626, an edict of Louis XIII, wanted by Richelieu, makes duelling punishable by death. Duels are decimating the nobility; the Cardinal wants swords in the king's service, not quarrels.
dict.François de Montmorency-Bouteville, duel: François de Montmorency-Bouteville, a famous duellist, fights on the Place Royale in May 1627. Despite his name and the pleas, he is beheaded on the Place de Grève on 22 June 1627: the edict applies to all.
dict.Compagnie créée par Louis XIII en 1622,: Company created by Louis XIII in 1622, blue tabard with a white cross. The rivalry with the Cardinal's guards, in red, is a reality of the court… that literature would amplify.
dict.Garde à coquilles percées et branches mu: Guard with pierced shells and many branches, associated with General Pappenheim, a figure of the Thirty Years' War raging in Germany in 1633.
dict.Dans le Paris de ce jeu, des êtres à éca: In the Paris of this game, scaled beings live hidden among men. Hard skin, claws that break the guard… and legs like anyone's. Pure game legend.
dict.Apercevoir une vouivre dans le ciel: Spot a wyvern in the sky

dict.En novembre 1630, la reine mère Marie de: In November 1630, the queen mother Marie de Médicis believes she has obtained Richelieu's dismissal. Louis XIII keeps him: she leaves the court, then flees in 1631 to the Spanish Netherlands.
